title: Replace Internet Identity UI with native username/password session auth and update admin gating

requirements.summary: Add username/password Sign Up + Sign In UI and a persistent session-based auth state (no email verification).
acceptanceCriteria: The app provides a dedicated Sign In page and a Create Account (Sign Up) flow.
Sign Up requires at minimum: username + password (and password confirmation).
No email collection or email verification is required anywhere in the UI or backend.
After successful Sign Up, the user can Sign In with the created username/password and is treated as authenticated across the app until they sign out.
Passwords are never stored or returned in plaintext by the backend (store only a salted/hashed representation).

file_operations.description: Create a session-auth React context/provider that manages username/password sign-in state, persists a backend-issued session token in localStorage/sessionStorage, provides signUp/signIn/signOut helpers, and exposes isAuthenticated + basic session info to the UI.
Add a small hook/util layer for reading/writing the session token and deriving authenticated state without depending on Internet Identity.

Implement the dedicated Sign In page UI (username + password) that calls the new session auth hook to obtain and store a session token; include clear English errors on invalid credentials; include navigation to Sign Up.

Implement the Create Account (Sign Up) page UI (username, password, confirm password) that calls session auth signUp and then guides the user to sign in (or auto-signs in if the backend supports it), with no email fields anywhere.

Replace Internet Identity login/logout handling with session-based Sign In/Sign Out behavior: when signed out, navigate to Sign In; when signed in, clear the session token and clear React Query cached data.

Update the frontend backend interface typings to include username/password auth capabilities (e.g., signUp, signIn, signOut/getSession) returning/accepting a session token; ensure no types expose plaintext passwords beyond client-to-backend submission.

requirements.summary: Update user order browsing to use the session identity so dashboards show only the signed-in user’s orders and order detail access is blocked when not owned (unless admin).
acceptanceCriteria: When a signed-in user creates an order, the order is associated with that authenticated user identity (not the Internet Identity principal).
Dashboard order list shows only orders for the currently signed-in user session.
Order detail page blocks access if the order is not owned by the current signed-in user session (unless the session is an admin session).
Admin panel can list all orders and update any order’s status using an admin session.

file_operations.description: Update order creation to include the current session token when calling the backend protected order-creation capability; ensure failures surface as clear UI errors (e.g., unauthorized when signed out).
Update the user-orders query to call the backend capability that returns orders for the current session token (instead of relying on principal-based ownership).
Update order detail fetching to include the session token so the backend can enforce ownership/admin authorization; treat unauthorized responses as a 'not found / no permission' UI state.
Ensure unauthorized order access produces the existing 'doesn't exist or you don't have permission' state based on session-based authorization errors (including non-owner access).
Ensure order submission works under session auth by relying on the updated create-order hook; keep existing ROLEPLAY-ONLY disclaimers and watermark behavior unchanged.

Align typings for order capabilities to support session-token authorization on user-protected operations (create order, list my orders, get order detail) while preserving existing Order model usage in the UI.

requirements.summary: Add Sign In/Sign Up routes and update all UI copy/navigation to remove Internet Identity prompts and direct users to username/password sign-in.
acceptanceCriteria: A new route exists for Sign In (and Sign Up if separate), and it is reachable from signed-out states.
Any UI that previously instructed users to use “Internet Identity” is updated to refer to signing in with username/password (English copy).
AuthGate no longer renders a button that triggers Internet Identity login; instead it directs the user to the Sign In page.
Brand header authentication controls support: Sign In (when signed out) and Sign Out (when signed in), based on the new auth state.
Landing page “How It Works” step text is updated to match the new sign-in method (username/password).

file_operations.description: Register new routes for /signin and /signup, and update index routing decisions to use session-auth state (not Internet Identity). Ensure Sign In/Up routes are reachable when signed out and protected areas still use AuthGate.

Replace Internet Identity gating with session-auth gating: when signed out, present English copy referencing username/password and provide a CTA that navigates to the Sign In route (no Internet Identity login button).
Update header navigation to use session-auth state for showing Dashboard/Admin links and for rendering Sign In/Sign Out behavior via the updated AuthStatusButton.
Update the 'How It Works' Step 1 text to say users sign in with username/password (remove 'Internet Identity' wording). Keep existing roleplay disclaimers intact.

requirements.summary: Update admin gating and navigation to use session-based admin role checks under the new username/password system.
acceptanceCriteria: Backend supports determining whether the current session token corresponds to an admin user (e.g., an isAdmin flag or role).
Frontend AdminGate uses the new backend admin check (based on the session token) to allow/deny access to /admin.
A signed-in admin user sees the Admin navigation entry and can access the Admin Panel successfully.
A signed-in non-admin user receives an “Access Denied” state on /admin.

file_operations.description: Update the admin check query to use the current session token and call the backend capability that verifies admin role for that session. This role-based behavior is backed by the selected "authorization" component on the backend; verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.
Ensure AdminGate authorization decisions are based on the session-token admin check and show the existing Access Denied UI for non-admin sessions.
Ensure the Admin navigation entry is only shown for admin sessions (using the session-based isAdmin check).
Update typings to include session-based role/admin-check capability used by AdminGate and admin navigation (consistent with the new username/password session auth model).
